9.55000,33.90000.name: Approval of release into the environment of Corn
9.55000,33.90000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-118.53300,34.17050.name: Tree of Life Center for Fertility, California Fertility Clinics
-118.53300,34.17050.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Vuk Jovanovic, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

7.39860,9.07650.name: National Biosafety Management Agency (Nigeria)
7.39860,9.07650.desc: Nigeria’s biosafety regulator, which has approved Bt cowpea — an engineered staple developed for African smallholders rather than for export commodity production. Nigeria is the largest market in West Africa, so approvals here shape what neighbouring regulators do next, and this is one of the few cases where the crop in question is what poor farmers actually grow and eat. Created by the NBMA Act 2015. It cleared Bt cotton in 2018, pod-borer resistant cowpea in 2019 — the first engineered food crop approved anywhere in Africa — and four TELA maize varieties in January 2024, and issued Africa's first genome-editing guidelines in 2020. Its public database shows 33 varieties cleared against four in commercial cultivation.

5.10800,52.09000.name: Rabobank
5.10800,52.09000.desc: The largest agricultural lender in the world, financing farms, traders and processors across dozens of countries, and publishing the sector analysis the industry plans against. Credit decides which farms can carry the cost of a seed-and-chemical package, which is a stronger filter on adoption than approval is.

57.57040,-20.27590.name: Noveprim
57.57040,-20.27590.desc: A long-tailed macaque breeding operation in Mauritius, and the single farm a major laboratory-animal buyer identifies by name among its monkey suppliers. That is the whole reason it belongs on this map. The same buyer's report describes enhanced due diligence, documentation, monitoring and auditing across its suppliers, and names one of them; farms reported elsewhere as sitting in the same chain are not listed. Mauritius has been the main non-Asian source of research macaques for decades, which makes it the part of the trade a purchaser can point to when asked where the animals come from.

15.43950,47.07070.name: Kilobaser
15.43950,47.07070.desc: An Austrian company selling a benchtop DNA and RNA synthesiser — a machine rather than a service. It ships in a wooden crate weighing about 27 kilograms, runs on nitrogen or argon gas, produces custom oligos in under two hours at 2.5 minutes a base, and can be operated entirely offline, which the company presents as a data security feature. Its customers include laboratories in Brazil, India and elsewhere. The reason this belongs beside the gene synthesis companies rather than among them: those companies screen the sequences they are asked to make and check who is ordering, and that screening works because the order has to pass through them. A machine on a bench removes that step entirely. Analyses cited by the industry itself suggest benchtop capacity could reach a tenth to a fifth of total gene synthesis within a decade.

5.65000,52.45000.name: Grazelands Rewilding
5.65000,52.45000.desc: The organisation now named alongside the European rewilding body as running the aurochs back-breeding work in practice — the day-to-day herd management across the breeding sites, distinct from both the foundation that started the programme and the network that supplies the land. It is worth recording separately because this facet's venture-funded companies are single corporations doing everything, while the back-breeding side is three or four bodies each holding one function: the science, the herds, the ground, and the genetics. Whether that division is a weakness or the reason the programme has run for nearly two decades is a question a reader can now put to both models from the same map.
